# Decisions: typescript-7

- 2026-08-29T17:40:08.978Z — chose **Upgrade the root devDependency typescript 6.0.3 to ^7.0.2, the native Go compiler port. Verified end to end before committing: typecheck clean on both workspaces, vitest 1718 passed / 4 skipped across 100 files (byte-identical to the TS 6.0.3 baseline taken minutes earlier), and build.mjs declaration emit produces 23 of 26 dist files byte-for-byte unchanged. Typecheck wall time 1.92s to 0.52s, a 3.7x speedup. npm pulls a platform-specific native binary alongside (on this machine node_modules/@typescript/typescript-darwin-arm64).** over Staying on 6.0.3 until 7.1 stabilises; or adopting @typescript/native-preview, whose latest is still a July 2026 dev build now superseded by the stable 7.0.2 on the latest tag. because The upgrade is provably invisible to everything sofar ships. tsc is used in exactly two places — noEmit typechecking and the L2 declaration emit in build.mjs — and never touches the esbuild bundles that are the actual published artifact, so all three JS bundles plus every runtime file hashed identical. The only delta is cosmetic: TS 7 preserves the source quote style in emitted string-literal types, so three d.ts files render readonly ['pass', 'findings'] where TS 6 rendered readonly ["pass", "findings"]. Those are the same type; no consumer can observe the difference. The config was already on the favorable side of the port — ES2022, ESNext, Bundler resolution, strict, noUncheckedIndexedAccess, isolatedModules, skipLibCheck, nothing legacy for the native compiler to reject. One behavioural difference found and worth knowing: TS 7 enforces forceConsistentCasingInFileNames against the invocation path where TS 6 normalised it away, so running tsc through a differently-cased path than the repo's canonical one (/Users/jins/io vs /Users/jins/IO on a case-insensitive macOS volume) raises TS1149 on files reached by relative import rather than through the workspace symlink. That is an invocation-path artifact, not a code defect: npm run typecheck runs from the package directory and is clean. Note the speedup is build- and editor-time only — it does nothing for the 26ms CLI hot path, which is Node executing esbuild output.
